unit.title: Introduction to Electrical Energy and DC Circuits

title: Dependent sources and passive circuit elements — R, L and C
summary: Dependent/controlled sources (VCCS, CCCS, CCVS, VCVS) and their equations; resistance, inductance and capacitance definitions, units and basic voltage-current relations.
transcription_policy: Notebook wording is preserved as far as it is safely readable. Crossed-out corrections are normalized to the final written reading; symbols and equations are transcribed into MathJax without adding unrecorded notebook content.

mapped_topics.label: Electrical energy sources: voltage, current, independent and dependent sources
Circuit elements: resistance, inductance and capacitance

blocks.text: If the voltage/current of a source depends upon some other voltage/current in the network, it is called a dependent/controlled source.

blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · VCVS dependent-source symbol

blocks.text: The property of a circuit element which opposes flow of current (R).
The property of a circuit element to oppose the change in current (L).
The inductance of a coil is defined as the ratio of flux linkage to the current flowing through the coil.
\(\phi\) = flux in weber; \(N\) = number of turns; \(i\) = current in amperes.
If the current across the inductor is constant, the inductor acts as a short circuit to DC.

blocks.alt: Notebook-style capacitor symbol with two straight parallel plates, horizontal leads, plus above the left plate and minus above the right plate.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Capacitor symbol

blocks.text: Any two conducting surfaces separated by an insulating dielectric exhibit the property of capacitance. Conducting surfaces are known as electrodes. Insulating substance is known as dielectric.
If the voltage across a capacitor is constant, capacitor acts as an open circuit to DC, i.e. \(i=0\).
